findings.current: So were the tires of the car spinning uselessly after slamming into the side of a bus.
findings.defect: The source also says the asphalt melting in the extreme heat was hot. That image is omitted.
findings.rationale: The Korean explicitly lists the melting asphalt, the spinning tires, and the narrator’s heart as hot.
findings.replacement: The asphalt melting in the extreme heat was hot, too. So were the tires of the car spinning uselessly after it slammed into the side of a bus.

findings.current: Then I grabbed the warm, pulpy thing my hand had touched and tore it out.
findings.defect: The translation omits the narrator silently looking at the Merman, which gives a short groan, before tearing out the pulpy object.
findings.rationale: The source includes both the Merman’s brief groan and the narrator’s silent look before the action; the accepted baseline preserves them.
findings.replacement: I silently looked at the Merman as it let out a short groan, then grabbed the warm, pulpy thing my hand had touched and tore it out.

findings.defect: The superior-looking Hunter’s spoken response, “Pardon? Ah, yes. Yes,” is missing.
findings.rationale: The source includes this startled acknowledgment before the narrator asks about the other areas, and the accepted baseline preserves it.

summary: The chapter is broadly faithful, but the assembled copy drops several concrete details and one spoken response preserved in the source and accepted baseline.
